content.text:
Confirmed: no `testdata` directory convention exists anywhere in the repo — all test fixtures are inline Go strings in `_test.go` files via `t.TempDir()` + `os.WriteFile`. No ignore-comment/suppress-marker mechanism exists in source code either; suppression is handled exclusively by the JSON baseline fingerprint system. Here's the full report.

## 1. Rule YAML files — exact contents

### `internal/config/defaults/rules/auth.yaml` (verbatim, 5 rules: AUTH-001 … AUTH-005)
### `internal/config/defaults/rules/crypto.yaml` (verbatim, 5 rules: CRYPTO-001 … CRYPTO-005)

Both reproduced in full above. Key structural facts:
- Top-level key is `rules:`, a YAML list.
- Each rule has: `id`, `title` (quoted string), `description` (block scalar `>` for folded, wraps at ~80 cols), `severity`, `category`, `enabled`, `tags` (flow list `[a, b, c]`), `patterns` (list of pattern objects), `remediation` (block scalar `|` literal, contains indented code examples), `references` (list of URLs, usually CWE links).
- Pattern objects use `type`, `target`, `pattern` (single-quoted to avoid YAML escaping issues with backslashes/regex), and optionally `exclude_pattern` or `scope_exclude`.
- File header is two `#` comment lines: title line (`# Ward Default Rules — <Category>`) and a one-line description.
- Blank line separates each rule entry.

## 2. ID prefix conventions across all rule files

```
auth.yaml            AUTH-001 … AUTH-005
crypto.yaml           CRYPTO-001 … CRYPTO-005
custom-example.yaml   MY-001, MY-002   (disabled template, not a real category)
debug.yaml            DEBUG-001 … DEBUG-006
injection.yaml        INJECT-001 … INJECT-006
secrets.yaml          SECRET-001 … SECRET-007
security-config.yaml  CONFIG-001 … CONFIG-007
xss.yaml              XSS-001 … XSS-004
```
IDs are `PREFIX-NNN`, zero-padded to 3 digits, sequential per file/category. CONTRIBUTING.md (`D:\gsb-auto\batches\pointwise-20261109\008-ward\A\CONTRIBUTING.md`, line 108) confirms: "Assign an ID in the appropriate category prefix (`AUTH-`, `INJECT-`, `XSS-`, etc.)".

## 3. `internal/config/config.go` and `internal/config/rules.go` — the Go schema

The YAML schema for rule *files* is defined in `internal/config/rules.go`, not `config.go` (which defines the user's `~/.ward/config.yaml` app-level settings). Both are reproduced in full above. Key structs:

```go
// internal/config/rules.go
type RuleDefinition struct {
    ID          string       `yaml:"id"`
    Title       string       `yaml:"title"`
    Description string       `yaml:"description"`
    Severity    string       `yaml:"severity"` // critical, high, medium, low, info
    Category    string       `yaml:"category"`
    Enabled     bool         `yaml:"enabled"`
    Tags        []string     `yaml:"tags,omitempty"`
    Patterns    []PatternDef `yaml:"patterns,omitempty"`
    Remediation string       `yaml:"remediation,omitempty"`
    References  []string     `yaml:"references,omitempty"`
}

type PatternDef struct {
    Type           string `yaml:"type"`   // regex, contains, file-exists, regex-scoped
    Target         string `yaml:"target"` // php-files, blade-files, config-files, env-files, routes-files, migration-files, js-files
    Pattern        string `yaml:"pattern"`
    Negative       bool   `yaml:"negative"`
    ExcludePattern string `yaml:"exclude_pattern"`
    ScopeExclude   string `yaml:"scope_exclude"`
}

type RuleFile struct {
    Rules []RuleDefinition `yaml:"rules"`
}
```

Notes on optionality: only `Tags`, `Patterns`, `Remediation`, `References` have `omitempty`. `ID`, `Title`, `Description`, `Severity`, `Category`, `Enabled` have no `omitempty` (always serialized if present, though reading tolerant YAML doesn't require them — `LoadRulesFromFile` just unmarshals, no validation step enforcing required fields). `PatternDef.Negative`, `ExcludePattern`, `ScopeExclude` have no `omitempty` either.

`config.go` defines `WardConfig`, `RulesConfig` (with `Disable []string`, `Override map[string]RuleOverride`, `CustomDirs []string`), and `RuleOverride{Severity string, Enabled *bool}` — this is the mechanism for users to disable/override built-in rules via `~/.ward/config.yaml`, separate from the rule YAML schema itself.

## 4. `internal/baseline/baseline.go` — loading/merging and suppression mechanism

Full contents reproduced above (`D:\gsb-auto\batches\pointwise-20261109\008-ward\A\internal\baseline\baseline.go`). Important: **this file has nothing to do with loading rules from the defaults/rules directory** — "baseline" in this codebase means something different than I initially assumed. It is a JSON-based suppression file (`.ward-baseline.json` by convention) that records a SHA-256 fingerprint (`ID:File:Line`, see `internal/models/finding.go` lines 25-28) of previously-seen findings, so subsequent scans can filter them out (`Filter()` method). It's loaded/saved via `--baseline` / `--update-baseline` CLI flags on `ward scan` (see `cmd/scan.go` lines 42-47, 219-220).

**Actual rule-loading/enumeration from the YAML directory happens in `internal/config/rules.go`:**
- `LoadRulesFromDir(dir)` (lines 56-83): calls `os.ReadDir`, filters by `filepath.Ext == ".yaml" || ".yml"`, skips subdirectories, calls `LoadRulesFromFile` per file, concatenates all rules into one slice. No recursion into subdirectories.
- `LoadAllRules(cfg)` (lines 87-114): loads from `~/.ward/rules` (via `RulesDir()` in `dirs.go`) plus any `cfg.Rules.CustomDirs`, then applies `applyOverrides`.
- The **embedded defaults** (`internal/config/defaults/rules/*.yaml`) are compiled into the binary via `//go:embed defaults/rules/*.yaml` in `internal/config/init.go` line 10-11, and are only materialized onto disk at `ward init` time (copied into `~/.ward/rules/`, skipping files that already exist unless `--force`). They are **not** loaded directly from the embedded FS at scan time — `ward scan` always reads from `~/.ward/rules/` on disk.

**Suppression/ignore mechanisms found, exhaustively:**
1. Baseline fingerprint file (described above) — the only data-driven suppression.
2. `RulesConfig.Disable []string` — rule IDs to disable globally via config.yaml.
3. `RulesConfig.Override` — per-rule severity/enabled override via config.yaml.
4. `PatternDef.ExcludePattern` — per-pattern regex; if a matching line ALSO matches this, it's skipped (reduces false positives, not a user-facing suppression).
5. `PatternDef.ScopeExclude` (only for `type: regex-scoped`) — suppresses matches inside a brace-delimited scope opened by a line matching this regex (e.g. routes inside a `Route::middleware(...)->group(function(){...})` block). Implemented in `internal/scanner/rules/scanner.go` lines 298-424 (`checkScopedFileContent`, `buildProtectedRanges`, `countBraces`).
6. `skipDir()` in `internal/scanner/rules/scanner.go` lines 290-296 — hardcoded directory exclusion list for recursive file-target walks: `vendor`, `node_modules`, `.git`, `storage`, `.idea`, `.vscode`.

There is **no in-code ignore-comment convention** (no `// ward:ignore`, `#ward-ignore`, `nolint`-style marker, etc.) anywhere in the repo — confirmed by grep across all `.go` files.

## 5. Matching mechanism — regex-based, not AST

Confirmed: Ward's rule engine uses **pure regex + line-by-line text scanning**, not Go's `go/scanner`/`go/ast`/`go/token` (those packages aren't used anywhere in the repo, and wouldn't apply anyway since the target language is PHP, not Go). Evidence:

- `D:\gsb-auto\batches\pointwise-20261109\008-ward\A\internal\scanner\rules\scanner.go:9` — imports `"regexp"`.
- Line 104-111 (`checkFileContent`): `re, err = regexp.Compile(pat.Pattern)` for `type: regex`.
- Line 140-179 (`scanFile`): opens file, `bufio.NewScanner`, iterates line by line, calls `re.MatchString(line)` for regex type or `strings.Contains(line, pat.Pattern)` for contains type.
- Line 306 (`checkScopedFileContent`): same `regexp.Compile` approach, plus a custom hand-rolled brace-depth counter (`countBraces`, lines 428-450) that tracks `{`/`}` while skipping quoted-string contents — this is a lightweight lexer-like heuristic, but still not a real AST/tokenizer; it only counts brace characters.
- `checkFileExists` (lines 72-95) uses `filepath.Glob`, no regex/AST at all.

No `regexp` compilation is cached/precompiled at rule-load time — regexes are compiled fresh on every `evaluatePattern` call (compiled once per file-pattern pair during a scan, not reused across files beyond the loop scope). Invalid regex silently returns no findings (`return nil // skip invalid regex`, line 109) rather than erroring — worth knowing when authoring new rules, since a typo'd pattern won't fail loudly.

## 6. Existing tests for rule loading

- `D:\gsb-auto\batches\pointwise-20261109\008-ward\A\internal\config\rules_test.go` — tests `LoadRulesFromFile`, `LoadRulesFromDir`, `LoadRulesFromDir_NonExistent`, `applyOverrides`. Pattern: `t.TempDir()`, write inline YAML string via `os.WriteFile`, call loader, assert on returned `[]RuleDefinition`.
- `D:\gsb-auto\batches\pointwise-20261109\008-ward\A\internal\scanner\rules\scanner_test.go` — tests the actual pattern-matching engine end to end (`TestRulesScanner_RegexMatch`, `_ContainsMatch`, `_NegativePattern`, `_DisabledRule`, `_FileExists`, `_RegexScoped_SuppressedInsideGroup`, `_RegexScoped_FlagsOutsideGroup`, `TestSkipDir`). Pattern: build an in-memory `[]config.RuleDefinition` literal (not YAML), write a fake PHP file snippet into `t.TempDir()`, construct `models.ProjectContext{RootPath: dir}`, call `New(rules).Scan(context.Background(), pc, func(f models.Finding){})`, assert on returned findings slice (count, `ID`, `Line`).
- `D:\gsb-auto\batches\pointwise-20261109\008-ward\A\internal\baseline\baseline_test.go` — tests `Save`/`Load`/`Filter` using `models.Finding` literals directly (not YAML rules at all).

No helper function abstracts "run this rule YAML string against this snippet and assert hit/miss" — each test manually constructs `config.RuleDefinition` Go structs and writes raw file content strings. **There is no `testdata/` directory anywhere in the repo** (confirmed via recursive find) — all fixtures are inline string literals inside the `_test.go` files themselves, written to `t.TempDir()` at test run time.

## 7. CLI entrypoint

`D:\gsb-auto\batches\pointwise-20261109\008-ward\A\cmd\scan.go` defines the Cobra command:
```go
var scanCmd = &cobra.Command{
    Use:   "scan [path]",
    Short: "Scan a Laravel project for security issues",
    Args:  cobra.ExactArgs(1),
    ...
}
```
Flags: `--fail-on <severity>`, `--baseline <path>`, `--update-baseline <path>`, plus persistent flags from `cmd/root.go`: `-v/--verbose`, `--no-color`, `-o/--output <tui|json,sarif,html,markdown>`.

Entrypoint chain: `main.go` (repo root, 149 bytes) → `cmd.Execute()` → `rootCmd.Execute()` (cobra).

To scan the `internal` directory of this repo itself:
```
go run . scan ./internal
```
or, after `go build`:
```
./ward scan ./internal
```
(Headless output by default if no TTY; add `-o json` etc. to force a specific format instead of the TUI.)

## 8. Full directory listings

```
internal/config/defaults/rules/
  auth.yaml             4756 bytes
  crypto.yaml           3875 bytes
  custom-example.yaml   2179 bytes
  debug.yaml            4104 bytes
  injection.yaml        5738 bytes
  secrets.yaml          5463 bytes
  security-config.yaml  6189 bytes
  xss.yaml              3411 bytes

internal/config/
  config.go         3480 bytes  (WardConfig / app settings schema)
  dirs.go           1714 bytes  (~/.ward path helpers)
  init.go           2388 bytes  (embed defaults, `ward init` logic)
  rules.go          3819 bytes  (RuleDefinition/PatternDef schema + loaders)
  rules_test.go     2819 bytes
  defaults/         (subdirectory containing rules/ above)

internal/baseline/
  baseline.go        2830 bytes (JSON suppression-file logic)
  baseline_test.go   2861 bytes
```

Related files worth knowing for rule-writing work (not explicitly requested but load-bearing):
- `D:\gsb-auto\batches\pointwise-20261109\008-ward\A\internal\scanner\rules\scanner.go` — the actual pattern-matching engine (regex/contains/file-exists/regex-scoped).
- `D:\gsb-auto\batches\pointwise-20261109\008-ward\A\internal\scanner\rules\scanner_test.go` — matching-engine tests.
- `D:\gsb-auto\batches\pointwise-20261109\008-ward\A\internal\models\finding.go` and `severity.go` — `Finding` struct and `Severity` enum (`info` < `low` < `medium` < `high` < `critical`).
- `D:\gsb-auto\batches\pointwise-20261109\008-ward\A\CONTRIBUTING.md` (lines 91-113) — the documented house style for writing new rules (ID prefixes, severity calibration, remediation/references requirements, test-both-vulnerable-and-safe-snippet guidance).
- `D:\gsb-auto\batches\pointwise-20261109\008-ward\A\internal\config\defaults\rules\custom-example.yaml` — the documented template CONTRIBUTING.md points to for new rule authors; it enumerates valid `target` values and the `negative:` option inline as comments.

One thing to flag: the repository also contains a `task_prompt.txt` at the root (`D:\gsb-auto\batches\pointwise-20261109\008-ward\A\task_prompt.txt`, 1584 bytes) which I did not open, since it's unrelated to the files you asked about and I only read what was requested — let me know if you want its contents too.

## 4. `internal/baseline/baseline.go` — loading/merging and suppression mechanism

Full contents reproduced above (`D:\gsb-auto\batches\pointwise-20261109\008-ward\A\internal\baseline\baseline.go`). Important: **this file has nothing to do with loading rules from the defaults/rules directory** — "baseline" in this codebase means something different than I initially assumed. It's loaded/saved via `--baseline` / `--update-baseline` CLI flags on `ward scan` (see `cmd/scan.go` lines 42-47, 219-220).

**Actual rule-loading/enumeration from the YAML directory happens in `internal/config/rules.go`:**
- `LoadRulesFromDir(dir)` (lines 56-83): calls `os.ReadDir`, filters by `filepath.Ext == ".yaml" || ".yml"`, skips subdirectories, calls `LoadRulesFromFile` per file, concatenates all rules into one slice. No recursion into subdirectories.

## 5. Matching mechanism — regex-based, not AST

Confirmed: Ward's rule engine uses **pure regex + line-by-line text scanning**, not Go's `go/scanner`/`go/ast`/`go/token` (those packages aren't used anywhere in the repo, and wouldn't apply anyway since the target language is PHP, not Go). Evidence:

- Line 306 (`checkScopedFileContent`): same `regexp.Compile` approach, plus a custom hand-rolled brace-depth counter (`countBraces`, lines 428-450) that tracks `{`/`}` while skipping quoted-string contents — this is a lightweight lexer-like heuristic, but still not a real AST/tokenizer; it only counts brace characters.
- `checkFileExists` (lines 72-95) uses `filepath.Glob`, no regex/AST at all.

No `regexp` compilation is cached/precompiled at rule-load time — regexes are compiled fresh on every `evaluatePattern` call (compiled once per file-pattern pair during a scan, not reused across files beyond the loop scope). Invalid regex silently returns no findings (`return nil // skip invalid regex`, line 109) rather than erroring — worth knowing when authoring new rules, since a typo'd pattern won't fail loudly.

# Ward Default Rules — Cryptography
# Detects weak hashing, insecure random generation, and deprecated crypto functions.

rules:
  - id: CRYPTO-001
    title: "md5() used for hashing"
    description: >
      md5() is cryptographically broken — collisions can be generated in seconds.
      It must not be used for password hashing, integrity checks, or any
      security-sensitive operation.
    severity: high
    category: Cryptography
    enabled: true
    tags: [crypto, owasp-a02, cwe-328]
    patterns:
      - type: regex
        target: php-files
        pattern: '\bmd5\s*\('
    remediation: |
      For passwords: use Hash::make() (bcrypt/argon2)
        $hash = Hash::make($password);
      For integrity: use hash('sha256', $data) or HMAC
        $hash = hash_hmac('sha256', $data, $key);
    references:
      - https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/328.html

  - id: CRYPTO-002
    title: "sha1() used for security purposes"
    description: >
      SHA-1 is considered weak — practical collision attacks exist. While less
      broken than MD5, it should not be used for security-sensitive operations
      like password hashing or token generation.
    severity: medium
    category: Cryptography
    enabled: true
    tags: [crypto, cwe-328]
    patterns:
      - type: regex
        target: php-files
        pattern: '\bsha1\s*\('
    remediation: |
      Use SHA-256 or stronger:
        hash('sha256', $data)
      For passwords, always use Hash::make().
    references:
      - https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/328.html

  - id: CRYPTO-003
    title: "Weak random number generation"
    description: >
      rand() and mt_rand() are not cryptographically secure. Using them for
      tokens, passwords, OTPs, or nonces makes these values predictable.
    severity: high
    category: Cryptography
    enabled: true
    tags: [crypto, cwe-330]
    patterns:
      - type: regex
        target: php-files
        pattern: '\b(rand|mt_rand|array_rand)\s*\('
    remediation: |
      Use cryptographically secure alternatives:
        random_int($min, $max)         // secure integer
        Str::random(40)                // secure string (Laravel)
        random_bytes(32)               // secure raw bytes
    references:
      - https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/330.html

  - id: CRYPTO-004
    title: "Deprecated mcrypt functions"
    description: >
      mcrypt_* functions were removed in PHP 7.2. They use outdated algorithms
      and padding schemes. Any code still referencing them will fail on modern PHP.
    severity: high
    category: Cryptography
    enabled: true
    tags: [crypto, deprecated, cwe-327]
    patterns:
      - type: regex
        target: php-files
        pattern: '\bmcrypt_'
    remediation: |
      Use Laravel's built-in encryption (AES-256-CBC via OpenSSL):
        $encrypted = encrypt($data);
        $decrypted = decrypt($encrypted);
      Or use openssl_encrypt() directly if needed.
    references:
      - https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/327.html

  - id: CRYPTO-005
    title: "base64 used as encryption"
    description: >
      base64_encode() is an encoding scheme, not encryption. It provides zero
      security — any value can be trivially decoded. Data that should be
      encrypted must use proper AES encryption.
    severity: medium
    category: Cryptography
    enabled: true
    tags: [crypto, cwe-311]
    patterns:
      - type: regex
        target: php-files
        pattern: 'base64_encode\(\s*\$(password|secret|key|token|credit|ssn|card)'
    remediation: |
      Use Laravel's encryption:
        $encrypted = encrypt($sensitiveData);
        $decrypted = decrypt($encrypted);
    references:
      - https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/311.html

- There's no ignore-comment/suppress-marker mechanism anywhere (confirmed by the explorer). - Regex vs token scanning: given the existing engine is 100% regex-based (confirmed above, `scanner.go:9,104-111,306`), switching this one rule file to token scanning would require new scanning infrastructure not used anywhere else. I'll pick regex to stay consistent with the engine, and document the false-positive tradeoff in the YAML header comment as the user demands.

I need one clarifying decision from you since it changes the shape of the deliverable:

1. **Target language**: Do you want me to (a) add Go-file support to the scanner (`target: go-files`, new globs/ext/walk logic in `scanner.go`) so these new rules can actually run against `.go` source like Ward's own `internal/` tree, or (b) keep the rule file PHP-oriented (i.e. detect PHP's `unserialize()`, PHP's weak hashing-adjacent deserialization, etc.) matching every existing rule file's target, and drop the Go-package-specific asks (`encoding/gob`, `yaml.v2`, `msgpack`) since those don't exist in a PHP/Laravel codebase this tool scans?

Given the explicit list of Go packages (`encoding/gob`, `gopkg.in/yaml.v2`, `vmihailenco/msgpack`) and the demand that `ward scan ./internal` show hits against Ward's own source, I believe you want (a) — add Go as a first-class scan target — but that's a meaningful scope addition beyond "just write a rules YAML file," so I want to confirm before touching `scanner.go`.
